contract: POST /api/worker/activity-tasks/{task}/acknowledge-cancellation (published Server 2.11, advertised as server_capabilities.activity_cancellation_acknowledgement, also in cluster info) records an activity worker's stop after a cooperative cancellation reached its attempt. The path is request-cancellation, then deliver-cancellation with call_kind activity from the workflow task, which cancels the attempt and records ActivityCancelled; the activity heartbeat then reports attempt_closed and the status route carries the cancellation_acknowledgement receipt with the request id. The acknowledgement answers 200 and records one ActivityCancellationAcknowledged event with the stop's evidence and the cancelled task's snapshot; the receipt then reads stopped and a repeat answers duplicate with the same event, while later outcomes stay refused. Before the request, with another request id or after an immediate cancel it answers cancellation_request_mismatch; before delivery activity_cancellation_not_recorded; for an older attempt of the execution activity_cancellation_acknowledgement_fence_mismatch. Ownership is checked in PHP's order with its bodies, then the claim: an attempt polled on protocol 1.19 cannot acknowledge. A request below protocol 1.20 is refused before validation; missing, non-string or over-long fields fail Laravel's validation. A run terminated after delivery still records the late stop, after its terminal event. Published 2.11.1 delivers a retried activity's cancellation to the execution's first task (Workflow #923), so that attempt's acknowledgement is refused as not fenced; the contract accepts exactly that reference defect or the correct acknowledgement. Embedded applications have no worker protocol.
